claim: The 2020 U.S. Census counted 5,205,461 Chinese except Taiwanese people alone or in combination
evidence: Official Detailed Demographic and Housing Characteristics File summary
geography_and_population: United States; self-identified detailed Asian groups
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Definition differs from Chinese alone and from Pew harmonized microdata
product_implication: Use as a defensible demographic universe; never call all of it affluent or reachable

claim: A current published tabulation places the Chinese American population around 5.5m; 58% of age 25+ have BA+; median household income is US$102,800
evidence: Pew synthesis of 2021–23 ACS and Pew survey sources
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Pew also reports a harmonized estimate near 5.04m; income is not individual WTP
product_implication: Supports U.S. scale and ability-to-pay tail; does not prove BaZi demand

claim: Chinese American households have unusually high income inequality; the 2022 90/10 ratio was 19.2
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Household-size-adjusted pooled data; not an individual buyer screen
product_implication: Do not treat Chinese identity as an affluent segment; qualify on trigger and ability to pay

claim: Canada counted 1,715,775 Chinese people in 2021; 97.7% lived in metropolitan areas and 69.5% in Toronto or Vancouver
evidence: Statistics Canada portrait using 2021 Census and later surveys
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Pandemic timing affects some labor results
product_implication: Toronto/Vancouver is the strongest second geography

claim: Among Chinese Canadians age 25–54, 61.8% had BA+; 41.3% of workers were professionals or senior/specialized managers
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: High education coexists with job mismatch and weaker belonging for some
product_implication: Supports professional ICP while migration transition remains a plausible job

claim: England and Wales counted 445,646 Chinese people in 2021
evidence: UK Government Ethnicity Facts and Figures downloadable census table
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Not the whole UK; Scotland and Northern Ireland require separate censuses
product_implication: UK is a smaller later market

claim: Scotland counted 47,075 Chinese people in 2022
evidence: Scotland Census detailed release and chart data
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Different census year from England/Wales
product_implication: Add only when forming a UK directional total

claim: Northern Ireland counted 9,495 Chinese people in 2021
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Small absolute population
product_implication: No launch priority

claim: Australia counted 1,390,639 people with Chinese ancestry in 2021, about 5.5%
evidence: Australian Bureau of Statistics cultural diversity release
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Only 549,618 were mainland-China-born; ancestry overstates Mandarin/mainland closeness
product_implication: Use a tighter birthplace/language screen for premium targeting

claim: New Zealand counted 279,039 Chinese people in 2023; 194,484 lived in Auckland
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Multi-ethnic people can appear in multiple groups
product_implication: Dense but small remote expansion

claim: Chinese residents were 74.3% of Singapore residents in 2020
evidence: Singapore Census of Population 2020 Statistical Release 1
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Share is older than 2025 resident total; local Chinese are not a migration-transition segment
product_implication: Singapore is culturally familiar and affluent but requires localized positioning

claim: Singapore had 4.2045m residents in 2025
evidence: Singapore Department of Statistics Population Trends 2025
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Multiplying by the 2020 Chinese share is an inference
product_implication: Directional Chinese resident universe is about 3.12m

claim: Malaysia had about 30.9m citizens and a 22.4% Chinese share in 2025, implying roughly 6.92m Chinese citizens
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: The Chinese share comes from a related 2025 demographic release; price and income differ greatly from Singapore
product_implication: Large later expansion but needs lower localized pricing

claim: Mainland China had 953.8m urban permanent residents in 2025
evidence: National Bureau of Statistics annual communiqué
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Urban residence is not affluence, category openness, or addressable demand
product_implication: Only an input to a heavily assumption-driven mainland proxy

claim: The national high-income quintile had RMB103,778 per-capita disposable income in 2025
evidence: National Bureau of Statistics income release
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Quintile average is not a premium-service buyer count and includes broad geography
product_implication: Use only as ability-to-pay context

claim: A CMB/Bain model estimated 3.16m people with RMB10m+ investable assets in 2022
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Commercial model; older; far narrower than affluent professionals
product_implication: Use as a strict alternate wealth anchor, not a launch forecast

claim: Academic survey synthesis reported 47% fengshui belief and 62% concern about auspicious dates in China
geography_and_population: Mainland Chinese adults; underlying survey years vary
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Fengshui and auspicious dates are not BaZi purchases; some data are older
product_implication: Category familiarity is not paid demand

claim: US$1 equaled about RMB6.78–6.79 at the research cut-off
evidence: China Foreign Exchange Trade System reference page
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Daily rate fluctuates; settlement fees differ
product_implication: Market model uses 6.79 only as a transparent conversion convention

claim: The selected higher-income-market Chinese population denominator is about 12.512m
evidence: U.S. 5.5m + Canada 1.715775m + UK 0.502216m + Australia 1.390639m + NZ 0.279039m + inferred Singapore 3.1239435m
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: National definitions differ; it includes all ages/incomes and local Singapore Chinese, so it is neither a high-income-person count nor strictly diaspora
product_implication: Use only as a top-down denominator

claim: The base initial North American screened demographic is about 920,559
evidence: U.S. and Canada population × assumed age shares × education proxies × assumed metro and cultural-language closeness
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: U.S. 58% BA+ is for age 25+ and is extrapolated to an assumed 25–54 slice; Taiwanese-origin coverage is definition-dependent
product_implication: Replace with interview and funnel data

claim: Base structural North American category SAM before channel reach models about 20.7k annual buyers/cases and US$4.97m
evidence: 920558.5 × 30% life event × 25% serious-service openness × 30% annual category purchase × one case × US$240 blended case AOV
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: This is category activity, not Zhiji revenue or the US$388/488 core price
product_implication: Apply explicit brand/channel reach and treat the range rather than midpoint as the insight

claim: A realistic year-3 outcome is capacity and trust constrained, not TAM constrained
evidence: 180 / 750 / 2,500 delivered cases at realized blended revenue per case US$328 / US$438 / US$550 imply about US$59k / US$329k / US$1.375m
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Cases, product mix, prices, practitioner supply, and demand are unvalidated
product_implication: Current evidence supports a boutique/productized practice, not venture scale

claim: Base launch-year reachable North American category opportunity models about 2,071 annual buyers/cases and US$0.50m
evidence: Top-down base structural category SAM × 10% qualified reachable-channel haircut
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Reach is an explicit hypothesis and must not be proxied by views, MAU, or group membership; Zhiji must still earn a share
product_implication: Replace the 10% assumption with a bottom-up model using channel-level qualified exposure and measured paid conversion

claim: The 20–43m mainland affluent selected-city adult proxy is reproducible only through explicit age, income, and city assumptions
evidence: 953.8m urban × 35–45% age 28–54 × 20% top-income × 30–50% selected-city concentration = about 20.0–42.9m
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Age and city-concentration factors are hypotheses; public data do not provide the exact cross-tab
product_implication: Treat mainland TAM as option value, not launch SAM

claim: Thirty percent of U.S. adults consult astrology, tarot, or fortune tellers annually, but 20% do so just for fun and only 6% rely at least a little for major decisions
evidence: Nationally representative Pew survey of 9,593 U.S. adults
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Not BaZi-specific; broad combined category; reliance differs from consultation
product_implication: Strong counterevidence to a broad affluent decision-advisory thesis

claim: Fifteen percent of Asian American adults reported annual fortune-teller use in the Pew survey
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Asian is broader than Chinese; no spend or premium WTP
product_implication: Shows category behavior exists but cannot size Zhiji

claim: Younger and lower-income U.S. adults were more likely category users
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Association is not causation and category is broad
product_implication: Contradicts a simple affluent-professional adoption assumption

claim: Astrology use includes identity, self-understanding, entertainment, and some professional decision use
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Preliminary; Western astrology rather than BaZi; not a market-size study
product_implication: Position around a bounded second lens, not a universal answer

claim: Divination often clarifies the present and manages uncertainty rather than simply predicting
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Theoretical and historical evidence does not prove consumer conversion
product_implication: Supports reflection and uncertainty language

claim: Public language shows explicit aversion to object/remedy upsells
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Single thread; not representative
product_implication: Publish a no-remedy no-affiliate pledge

claim: A public Dcard account reports trying free content then paying US$68 for an 8,000-word report
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: One buyer; no independent verification of service quality
product_implication: Proof-before-purchase can work, but report length is commoditized

claim: A media test buyer paid RMB385 and reported calibration details were inaccurate; the provider initiated a refund
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Dated and one case
product_implication: A defined fit/refund process can build trust more credibly than accuracy claims

claim: A public report describes high repeated metaphysics-app spend during job insecurity
evidence: TMTPost account of a mainland technology worker
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: One reported anecdote; not prevalence; spending may reflect harm
product_implication: Frequency caps and crisis safeguards are essential; do not treat compulsive LTV as success

claim: No reliable public dataset was found for paid BaZi use, premium WTP, conversion, CAC, repeat, or revenue among affluent overseas Chinese professionals
evidence: Search across government, academic, first-party competitors, app stores, marketplaces, and public discussions
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Absence of found evidence is not proof no data exists
product_implication: Primary paid experiments are required before platform investment

claim: Some high-intent buyers simultaneously want non-exploitative service and predictive accuracy
evidence: The same Singapore shopper rejected object upsells, requested blind-spot insight, and asked for accurate analysis/predictions; a Dcard buyer valued a reference framework while judging accuracy
publication_or_live_date: Public comment visible as one year old on access date
geography_and_population: Singapore public forum; separate Dcard account in Taiwan/Hong Kong
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Anecdotes, not prevalence; the row URL supports the Singapore example only
product_implication: Ethical non-determinism may lower conversion among incumbent-category buyers and must be tested

claim: Master Sean Chan lists US$588 single-chart, US$888 two-chart, US$1,288 private, and US$200 Q&A
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Visible price does not reveal volume or conversion
product_implication: Established named authority sets a premium ceiling, not Zhiji's launch price

claim: Joey Yap's booking system lists US$298 for a team consultant; founder service is quote-only
evidence: Live first-party booking and pricing pages
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: No audited sales volume; principal and associate demand differ
product_implication: US$298 is a strong mainstream human-service anchor

claim: Way Fengshui lists practitioner tiers from about S$204.92 to S$1,839.92 with annual reviews
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Promotions and local tax/currency context; no transaction volume
product_implication: Shows transparent tiering and annual episodic retention

claim: Master So lists HK$12,800 full and HK$5,800 annual readings
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Celebrity authority; audio-only; sales volume unknown
product_implication: High prices monetize status and name, not software

claim: LingYuan AI lists RMB9.9 single, RMB39.9 monthly, and RMB299 annual products
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Regulatory and scale status unverified
product_implication: Automated Chinese reports are a low-price commodity

claim: FateTell's web shop lists US$39.99 FateBook and US$19.99 FortuneBook
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Shop price is not proof of buyers or trust; app subscription prices are separate
product_implication: Polished AI output cannot be Zhiji's moat

claim: The established official 问真八字 product offers multi-platform professional charting, cloud cases, true-solar-time support, classical/reference material, and AI hints
evidence: Official product download page and browser tool
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Current official comparable price was not captured; unrelated lookalike App Store listings must not be attributed to this product
product_implication: Calculation depth is table stakes, but current pricing/scale cannot be inferred

claim: Fiverr displayed 143 BaZi services, commonly around US$5–80+
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Listing count is supply, not transaction volume; sellers may use AI
product_implication: Establishes price pressure on generic reports

claim: Etsy displays many BaZi PDFs from about US$3.99 to US$209, with many in US$8–65 range
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Discounts, search personalization, and reviews do not reveal total market
product_implication: Decision-specific PDF products are easy to copy

claim: CHANI lists US$11.99/month and US$107.99/year
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Western astrology ritual subscription differs from episodic BaZi consultation
product_implication: Voice and editorial trust are relevant; daily subscription mechanics are not

claim: Co–Star sells low-cost à la carte readings and a subscription while users compare outputs with free AI
evidence: Official app/product pages and App Store reviews
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Review theme is not population prevalence
product_implication: LLMs cap willingness to pay for generic generated prose

claim: At least 47 direct, adjacent, marketplace, app, and substitute competitors were identified
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Not exhaustive; price and policy pages change
product_implication: Market is crowded; integrated human accountability is the white space

claim: FateTell's U.S. App Store lists US$59.99/year and US$4.99/week products
evidence: Apple App Store first-party distribution listing
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: App and web purchases/benefits can differ; ratings are not users
product_implication: Keep platform-specific prices separate

claim: FateTell's App Store privacy promise and its detailed policy create a material wording tension about third-party data sharing
evidence: The policy says certain inputs go to OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google, while app marketing uses an absolute no-sharing phrase
geography_and_population: Global users / Hong Kong storage / U.S. AI vendors
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: The policy also provides controls and says API data are not used for training by default; tension is wording, not proof of unlawful conduct
product_implication: Zhiji must use literal task/vendor disclosure and avoid absolute privacy claims

claim: BetterUp for Individuals stopped new purchases and is winding down through January 2027
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: BetterUp enterprise continues; wind-down does not invalidate the broader coaching substitute
product_implication: Do not use BetterUp individual plans as a current purchasable price benchmark

claim: Yan Fengshui lists SGD188 yearly, SGD368 full, and SGD528 bundle prices effective January 2026
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Visible prices do not show volume; 70% conditional refund is on a separate policy page
product_implication: Supports transparent annual-review and local human-price anchors

claim: The ICF reported a US$272 average one-hour coaching fee in North America for 2022
evidence: ICF 2023 Global Coaching Study executive summary
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Coaching is an adjacent credentialed category; average is not direct consumer price for all coaches
product_implication: At US$400+ Zhiji competes with action-oriented credentialed help

claim: A US$388 core case models about US$159 gross profit before CAC and 43% of net sales under stated labor/cost assumptions
evidence: 5% refund allowance; 2.9% + US$0.30 fee; US$7 software; 3.25 practitioner hours at US$55; 0.5 admin hour at US$25
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: All cost, time, refund, and CAC inputs are unvalidated
product_implication: US$388 is a validation price, not yet a sustainable target

claim: A US$488 case models about US$251 pre-CAC gross profit and 54% of net sales using the same workflow
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Price acceptance is unknown; labor may rise with expectations
product_implication: Test US$488 after 10–20 cases if quality and acceptance hold

claim: Monthly subscription is a poor first fit for serious decision cases
evidence: Direct human services are episodic; adjacent subscriptions depend on daily/weekly ritual; dependency and renewal risks add harm and friction
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Some buyers may value annual review; repeat behavior is untested
product_implication: Use one-off cases and later annual review, not daily engagement

claim: The strongest plausible early moat is a consented longitudinal calibration-and-outcome ledger plus practitioner QA and referrals
evidence: Sampled competitors do not visibly combine versioned calculation, preregistered calibration, human sign-off, and delayed outcome review
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Every feature is copyable; the data moat does not exist until substantial high-quality cases accrue
product_implication: Do not market a data moat or scientific proof before it exists

claim: The initial category should retain BaZi in the label and use decision language as the benefit
evidence: Competitors and public shoppers use BaZi reading, 八字咨询, 命书, or master; adjacent coaching owns decision/advisory language
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: No controlled message test has yet been run
product_implication: Test Private BaZi consultation for major life transitions against alternatives

claim: Los Angeles Municipal Code §43.30 contains an on-books prohibition on advertising or carrying on fortune-telling through astrology, numerology, oriental mysteries, and similar means
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Text alone does not determine enforceability or application to exact remote-service facts
product_implication: Local counsel and licensing review are a pre-payment gate

claim: The California Supreme Court invalidated a materially similar paid-fortune-telling ban under the California free-speech clause
evidence: Spiritual Psychic Science Church v. City of Azusa, 39 Cal.3d 501
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Old precedent and different ordinance/facts; practical enforcement and licensing still require counsel
product_implication: Correct conclusion is legal uncertainty, not definite prohibition or safety

claim: The FTC can challenge deceptive AI, capability, scientific, accuracy, testimonial, and outcome claims
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Application depends on exact general impression and evidence
product_implication: No scientific astrology, accuracy rate, guaranteed outcome, or false human-only claim

claim: The FTC Consumer Reviews and Testimonials Rule restricts fake reviews, sentiment-conditioned incentives, undisclosed insiders, and certain suppression
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Specific application requires facts; honest incentives may still need disclosure
product_implication: Ask for reviews regardless of sentiment and publish delayed evidence without cherry-picking

claim: California companion-chatbot law creates duties for relational AI, while bounded productivity/analysis tools are excluded
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Classification depends on design and actual use
product_implication: No persistent master persona or emotional companion

claim: China's PIPL has extraterritorial scope for specified processing and heightened sensitive/cross-border obligations
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Exact transfer mechanism and product application require China counsel
product_implication: Do not deliberately serve mainland users in MVP

claim: China's 2025 clean-internet campaign explicitly targeted online paid fortune-telling and related content
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Campaign scope and enforcement vary; not a complete legal opinion
product_implication: Mainland acquisition cannot be a launch dependency

claim: China's anthropomorphic AI interaction rules effective 2026-07-15 restrict dependency, manipulation, unreasonable decisions, and require safety, privacy, and labeling controls
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Scope depends on sustained anthropomorphic/emotional interaction
product_implication: An AI companion or autonomous master is strategically and legally poor

claim: Apple treats fortune-telling apps as a saturated category and may reject new apps unless they provide a unique, high-quality experience
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Submission review is case-specific; existing apps do not guarantee acceptance
product_implication: Use web-first MVP and defer native app

claim: PayPal APM and Braintree expressly restrict psychic or fortune-teller services; Stripe's current U.S. list does not name a blanket category ban but requires legal, nondeceptive, accurately underwritten activity
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Account-specific underwriting can be stricter and terms change
product_implication: Obtain written processor approval and never disguise the business

claim: TikTok permits fortune-telling ads only in specified markets and without exact predictions, guarantees, or definitive solutions
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Campaign review can be stricter; other sensitive targeting rules also apply
product_implication: Paid social copy must be neutral, non-deterministic, adult, and geo-bounded

claim: UK GDPR can treat health, beliefs, sexuality, and sex-life material as special-category data and restrict solely automated significant decisions
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Exact lawful basis and DPIA need product facts
product_implication: UK launch needs localized consent, data minimization, and real human review

claim: PIPEDA applies to commercial activity and cross-border/interprovincial personal-information flows; context can make information sensitive
evidence: Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada guidance
geography_and_population: Canada outside substantially similar provincial regimes
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Alberta, BC, and Quebec have separate regimes
product_implication: Build meaningful consent and rights before Canada expansion

claim: Singapore's PDPA requires accountability, purpose, consent/notification, protection, retention, transfer, access/correction, breach response, and DPO controls
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Specific exemptions and consumer rules require local review
product_implication: Singapore is conditional, not frictionless

claim: Australia's federal privacy obligations depend partly on turnover and specified small-business categories; cross-border and sensitive-data rules apply to covered entities
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Small-business exemption is fact-specific and reform may change scope
product_implication: Do not assume exemption; apply premium privacy controls regardless

claim: New Zealand's Privacy Act can apply extraterritorially and requires a privacy officer; cross-border and indirect-collection rules may matter
evidence: New Zealand Privacy Commissioner information sheets
contradictory_evidence_or_limitation: Application depends on carrying on business and data facts
product_implication: Add NZ only after localized privacy operations
